entries.claim: 2026-10-C01: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, Method / verification and cost tables; PROTOCOL.md §1 and §4.3, capture-parity claim.
entries.replacement: Claude costs are derived from deduplicated Claude Code usage logs. Their completeness against independent provider accounting remains unvalidated, including for the subscription routes used here. Missing usage would understate those costs. Codex costs use logged cumulative counters; those counters do not independently establish complete capture. If the logs undercount, costs are understated, TIER scores read high, and Claude looks relatively cheaper in cross-vendor comparisons. Accounting consistency and reproducibility from captured evidence are the properties checked; capture parity against independent provider accounting is not proven. No historical cost multiplier or measured error bound is established.

For Claude Code 2.1.296, completeness against billed output remains unvalidated. We price the recorded output count without adding an inferred thinking count. The public bundles report no separate Claude reasoning count; not reported is not zero. Internal consistency of a log breakdown cannot independently establish completeness against provider accounting. The broader thinking-token consistency survey is not part of the public evidence and is not presented here as a publicly reproducible measurement.

The experimental unit is the complete model-tool configuration, including the recorded effort, tool permissions, caching policy and billing route. Cross-vendor cost comparisons describe only the tested configurations and tasks; they do not isolate model efficiency or establish a purchasing recommendation. The harness set no effort flag; effective effort was observable for 12 of 30 runs (3 high, 9 medium) and unobservable for 18. Claude Code and Muse ran from the operator's home and config directories under the harness's recorded isolation policy: Claude Code with customisation disabled by safe-mode and isolation flags, Muse with a settings-key allowlist and isolation flags (an inherited-trust residual remains); the other tools ran from a fresh config home. The four first-replicate Claude Code runs on 2026-10-12 carry the earlier stamp text 'customisation disabled by flags'. In those stamps, clean_config was written as a fixed true rather than measured; later stamps use a computed value. All twelve Claude Code stamps record safe-mode in their auth policy. The public stamps support the recorded policy, not an independently measured clean home. Every Claude Code run recorded one-hour cache writes, priced at 2x input: 28.5% of Haiku 5.5's spend, 38.0% of Fable 5.1's, 42.1% of Opus 5.5's and 49.5% of Sonnet 5.5's three-run spend. No Codex, OpenCode or Muse run recorded cache writes. Haiku 5.5 and gpt-6-luna share input/output list rates ($0.10/$0.50 per million); Fable 5.1 and gpt-6-astra share $10/$50. Their respective 8.6x and 5.0x cost-per-accepted differences describe the tokens and caching of model-tool configurations, not isolated model efficiency.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C04: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, Compared with Edition 1:369-374 and limitation 1, claimed top-of-order inversion.
entries.replacement: In Edition 1, claude-opus-4-8 had the higher observed mean cost on orgsync than claude-fable-5, but their run ranges overlap; three runs do not establish a stable ordering. For the two-sided exact permutation test of the difference in mean cost in Edition 1, with three runs per model, the observed p-value is 0.30 and the minimum achievable p-value is 0.10. This does not establish equivalence. Independence of July runs has not been established; the permutation p-value is a conditional calculation under that assumption. Sample means and table sorting do not establish stable population ordering. The Edition 1 inversion cannot be reused as established evidence of stable ordering.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C05: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, admission rule / The finding:26-31 and Compared with Edition 1:378-385, calibration selection.
entries.replacement: The three Edition 1 failures in this comparison are the calibration runs that admitted orgsync to service, at $0.527148, $0.563410 and $0.465123. They were reused as scored runs, not fresh held-out observations. The probability that the admission-selected panel contained a failure was 1 by construction. The Edition 2 successor passed this already published task; this comparison shows that the successor passed, does not measure how much the model line improved, and is not evidence that the task separates models. Fresh replicates do not make a calibration-selected task held out.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C06: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, Method / Known limitations; PROTOCOL.md §4.1 and §9, preregistration and N=1 claims.
entries.replacement: Historical exceptions and amendments are not prospective preregistration. Edition 2 increased N from 1 to 3 after all first results were known (R-2026-10-12-24), admitted GLM 5.3 Flash after the original 27 runs (R-2026-10-13-1), and corrected Sonnet cache-read report pricing after execution (R-2026-10-12-25). Its report table ultimately uses v13, while the original 27 bundles retain v11 and the three Flash bundles retain v13. These are disclosed post-result changes, not a wholly predeclared roster, replication schedule or frozen report-rate analysis. The older N=1 and never-add-replicates language does not describe the completed October panel. Original manifests and run bytes remain historical evidence. No enforced prospective lock or independent anchor is demonstrated by the published artifacts; future commitment/deviation enforcement is separate work, not a property conferred on this edition by this erratum.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C07: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, The finding:13, hidden test suite; PROTOCOL.md §5.4 hidden/never sees claims.
entries.replacement: These are operator-written acceptance tests, with commitment timing and prior-publication limitations disclosed. Independent means separate from the submitted program, not independent authorship or independent validation. Hidden at an invocation does not mean previously unseen: orgsync prompt and judge were public from 2026-07-23, before October scoring. Duration remained active with a public judge, and cronspec had a public judge without a recorded reveal event. Public availability establishes an opportunity for prior exposure, not proof of training inclusion. No paired unpublished constants-variant contamination control was demonstrated for any scored task. Published-task passes are historical task/configuration observations, not held-out capability evidence.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C08: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, How to read the tables, TIER column; The finding:14-16, 499x headline.
entries.replacement: The benchmark's TIER column is fixed task-difficulty points per $1,000 of captured AI usage priced at list rates. It differs from the product's TIER, which uses merged-work outcome points and its own eligibility and observed-quality rules. A benchmark acceptance is not a merged pull request; the values are not comparable with a product score. This is an observational ratio, not a causal estimate of AI productivity, value or return. The 499x cost ratio decomposes as about 100× from input/output rates × 3.3× total tokens ≈ 330×, with roughly another 1.5× from token mix. It is a descriptive spread for these configurations on this task, not a capability ranking.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C09: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md:19-23,645-651, dispersion and reliability; PROTOCOL.md §4.1 leading-indicator claim.
entries.replacement: M14 (first-call cache evidence): Independence of runs cannot be assumed: first-call cache evidence shows cache state carried between runs. The dispersion figures may misstate run-to-run variance; the direction was not measured. Under a two-sided exact permutation test with 3 runs per configuration, the smallest attainable p is 0.10 (2 of 20 arrangements), so no pairwise cost ordering reaches p≤0.05. That test also assumes independent runs, which cannot be assumed (M14), so no p computed this way is a valid probability. No cost ordering is established; only non-overlapping cost tiers are described. Dispersion as a leading indicator of the failure edge is an unvalidated hypothesis, not an established predictive relationship. Three costs per cell are descriptive observations, not a calibrated uncertainty interval or evidence of long-run reliability. In Edition 2, GLM 5.3 Flash had 46.2% dispersion and passed all three runs; that does not validate or refute a predictive rule. Neither an effective sample size nor the identity of any outside cache source was measured.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C10: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, verification instructions / Evidence preparation:734-736, harness's word.
entries.replacement: Default verification checks hashes, recorded usage/cost derivations and the implemented numeric table comparisons; it executes no submissions. A successful check does not establish every narrative fact, complete usage capture, judge validity, or production quality. Missing required artifacts or unavailable judges can be reported as SKIP while verification exits 0; a zero exit code alone does not mean every submission was rejudged. No third-party clean-rejudge receipt has been established. These editions are historical case studies with errata; no claim to reproduce the Model Report yourself or to independently re-execute its model runs is made.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C11: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, evidence preparation / commitment and hash guarantees.
entries.replacement: A reader without the original logs cannot prove their pre-redaction hashes from the redacted kit. Matching current hashes establishes consistency with the shipped bytes, not historical custody or commitment timing. Wall time rests on harness receipts. TASKS.md records that §5.6 escrow was not met, no independently anchored timestamp proof exists, and orgsync rep1's judge hash reached the ledger 4m34s after its first verdict. Commit history and post-judgment stamps cannot retroactively supply the missing pre-result guarantee. These limitations remain attached to both editions; this dated correction supplies neither an external timestamp nor a prospective commitment gate.

entries.claim: 2026-10-C15: editions/2026-10/REPORT.md, Reproduce the verification:699-704 and Evidence preparation:734-736, verification scope and rejudge instructions.
entries.replacement: Measured on 2026-10-16 in an exported --edition all kit from reviewed base commit 72a226e872715225df93424c802f09baa2bf4b17 with local review repairs, using the verifier hash in REJUDGE-RECEIPT.json: 30 verdicts reproduced (30 accepted, 0 rejected); RE-JUDGE 30 bundles · PASS 30 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 0. The two edition commands together reproduced 93 distinct archived outcomes; the exported July edition mirror was byte-checked against the root bundles and its 63 outcomes were rejudged once. Default verification executes no submissions. The opt-in --rejudge executes the archived model-written programs against their stamped, revealed acceptance judges on disposable copies; it does not re-run models or validate the judge, production quality, or capture completeness. Temporary copies and a reduced environment are not an operating-system sandbox. Missing required artifacts or unavailable judges are reported as SKIP; a zero exit code alone does not mean every submission was rejudged. --require-no-skips makes every such omission fail. These measured exported-kit runs had no OS network isolation. Only the Docker launcher provides network isolation; a bare-host run executes model-written code with the user's account and network. The exported rejudge-networkless.sh workflow runs with --network none, checks both editions with --require-no-skips and requires a planted flipped verdict to fail. No third-party clean-rejudge receipt has been established.
